analysis:
Examined the EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift change. It threads an optional stopStringScope (CBv2StopStringScope?) through runPump (head 15, 32) and pump (head 64) into matchedStopSequence (head 150-151). The parameter defaults to nil. It affects only the matched_stop_sequence metadata recorded on usageSignal for .stop/.length finishes. It does not touch KV reservation release, prefix-cache staging/receipt completion (T-041), native retirement, cancellation or encryption paths. Token replay (base 104-112) still excludes stop tokens.

A possible privacy consideration: scoping replay to non-reasoning spans reduces the risk that a reported stop sequence reveals withheld reasoning. This is a narrowing, not a regression.

The inference.md head units 16-17 (lines 2416-2981) are unchanged surrounding docs. The only doc change, at line 1866, describes Gemma4/<think> ReasoningStopScope and diffusion Gemma carrying no scope. It is consistent with the code plumbing.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump 2beb401f->5ffbb801 is opaque here. Its contents (CBv2StopStringScope, ReasoningStopScope, the engine stop holdback and any other engine changes) were not supplied. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

Integration should verify the following:
- Callers of runPump (EngineV2Bridge+Submission) pass the same scope used by the engine.
- matchedStopSequence in EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift handles a nil scope identically to the prior behavior.
- The submodule diff introduces no changes to KV/cache, attestation or memory admission paths (TB-007, T-041, T-028).

No threat-model update appears needed for this change itself.
